sections.heading: Tile vs. Asphalt Shingles, Slate, and Metal Roofs

c.v: Tile is one of the longest-lived roof types a Newark homeowner can choose, and one of the heaviest.

runs.v: Tile roofs can last over 50 years with proper care, with clay tile at 100 years or more and concrete tile at a typical 40 to 75 years; asphalt shingles last 20 to 30 years with proper maintenance; slate roofs are known for their lifetime durability; and metal roofs offer superior durability and energy efficiency at a fraction of tile's weight. The roofing materials also fail differently, which is why expert roof repair on tile looks nothing like replacing missing shingles on an asphalt roof: a missing shingle is slid in and nailed in minutes, while a broken tile has to be lifted out of an interlocking field without cracking its neighbors.

Replacement triggers differ by roof type as well. On an asphalt roof, roof replacement is often the best option for roofs over 20 years old or when granule loss exceeds 30%; on a tile roof over 20 years old, the tile is usually sound, and the major work is the underlayment beneath it. When full replacement is warranted, New Jersey's statewide Uniform Construction Code, enforced by each town's construction official, takes the place of separate local building codes, and an existing tile covering needs a full tear-off to the deck rather than a recover-over under N.J.A.C. 5:23-6.4.

sections.heading: How to Fix a Broken Roof Tile Without Replacing It

c.v: A hairline crack or a small chip in a roof tile can often be sealed in place, but only as a stopgap.

runs.v: The repair cleans and dries the tile, fills the crack or patches small holes with a compatible roofing sealant or tile adhesive, and color-matches the surface; patching small holes this way can stop small leaks for a season or two. It is not a fix for a tile with a missing piece, a crack across its full width, or a tile that has slipped, and no sealant helps once water has reached the underlayment. Stay off the roof surface, because foot traffic is a leading cause of broken tiles; binoculars from the ground show most damage safely.

Everything beyond a hairline crack is a replacement, and replacing one tile is a small job: the broken tile is lifted out, the fastener beneath is cut or pulled, and a matched tile slides into the course, at $50 to $300 per tile. Roof leak repair typically involves sealing the entry point, so the roof repair process on tile starts with a flashing inspection before the tile field, counts every penetration and transition, and treats flashing repairs as crucial to prevent water ingress at joints. A fantastic job on the tile field still leaks if the flashing at the chimney is wrong, which is why roof issues on tile are diagnosed layer by layer.

faqs.q: How long does a tile roof last in the New Jersey climate?

runs.v: Clay tile lasts 100 years or more and concrete tile a typical 40 to 75 years, per the InterNACHI life-expectancy chart and the Tile Roofing Industry Alliance, while the underlayment beneath the tile fails first. A 30-to-50-year-old tile roof commonly needs underlayment replacement beneath tiles that remain sound.

faqs.q: Should you repair or replace a tile roof?

runs.v: Repair a tile roof when the damage stays localized, and replace the tile cover when broken or displaced tiles cross roughly 20–25% for clay or 15–20% for concrete, or when the underlayment beneath has failed. A damage evaluation settles it, and a tile roof often needs only underlayment replacement beneath sound tiles, the cheaper path that preserves the original tile.

faqs.q: What happens if individual tiles crack or break?

runs.v: A cracked or broken tile is removed and replaced individually, at $50–$300 per tile, per HomeGuide data. Breakage typically traces to foot traffic and impact rather than material failure, and the replacement matches the existing profile and color.

faqs.q: Do tile roofs hold up to New Jersey freeze-thaw winters?

runs.v: Clay tile resists freeze-thaw well, while concrete tile carries spalling risk. Newark crosses the freezing point repeatedly through winter, so proper ventilation and underlayment management are essential, especially for concrete tile.
